title: Save your money, buy a home gym
summary: NH argues a home gym is one of the soundest financial decisions a lifter can make, not mainly because of saved membership fees but because of the time, energy and money lost travelling to and moving around a commercial gym. He adds resale value and greater commitment and consistency, and says you can start for 300-400 dollars.
claims: The usual membership-savings argument is weak: a 3000-dollar home gym against a 300-dollar yearly membership takes 10 years to pay off, which most people cannot picture
The hidden cost of a commercial gym is travel time: packing a bag, driving, parking, changing, showering adds about 1 h 10 min per session even with a gym 10 minutes away
For many novices, travel time equals training time, which helps explain why so many quit
Three hours of training plus three hours of travel per week is six hours of mental and physical drain
At 15 dollars an hour, losing 1 h 10 min three times a week is about 45 dollars a week of lost earnings
Gas, bus or train fares are additional hidden costs of a commercial gym
At his huge university gym it took 15-20 minutes from entrance to lifting and about 10 minutes to walk to the bathroom
Walking between machines and hunting for clips or handles takes a shocking share of commercial gym time; a small home gym removes it
Buying a home gym is like buying a house instead of renting: you own the equipment and can resell it, while a membership has no resale value
Even overpriced equipment saves money in the long run compared to memberships
Investing in physical equipment creates commitment, so home gym owners are more likely to stick with lifting consistently
You can start a home gym with 300-400 dollars
